title: The School Bag Is Still on the Floor | Parenting Rewind
description:
You have asked about the school bag four times and nobody is moving. A practical pause-and-rewind response for parents.

General parenting education; every child and family is different.
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: You have asked about the school bag four times and nobody is moving. A long list about shoes, lunch, teeth, and the bag can overwhelm a child who has not started step one. Before reacting, pause for one breath so the next words can be short, clear, and useful. Get attention and give one direction: Put your lunchbox in the bag; then wait and praise completion before the next step. One direction at a time makes success easier to see and easier to reinforce.

source.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: Steps for Giving Good Directions

claim_limits: The suggested wording is an example, not a guarantee.
Families should adapt expectations to age, development, safety and individual needs.
